questions.question_text:
A train’s speed-time graph rises linearly from 0 to 15 m s$^{-1}$ in 120 s, remains at 15 m s$^{-1}$ until 420 s, then falls to zero at 480 s.
Three statements are true and one is false.
Which is false?

options.text: During the first part of the journey the train is accelerating at $\frac18\,\text{m s}^{-2}$.
options.why: This is true: the initial gradient is $15/120=1/8$.

options.text: The distance between the two stations is $5.85\,\text{km}$.
options.why: This is true: the graph area is 5850 m.

options.text: When 240 seconds have elapsed the train has travelled half the distance between the two stations.
The train travels at constant speed for 5 minutes.
options.why: This is true: constant speed lasts from 120 s to 420 s.

questions.solution_text: The total distance is the area under the graph: $\frac12(120)(15)+(420-120)(15)+\frac12(60)(15)=5850\,\text{m}$. At 240 s the distance is $900+120(15)=2700\,\text{m}$, not half of 5850 m (2925 m), so the third statement is false.
